This isn't the appropriate server to discuss other blockchains or solicit thoughts/opinions on choices/tradeoffs of other platforms. it's a development server, it's the best place to study others work to try and improve on our own don't be a kid With that attitude, you're probably not getting far. 🤷‍♂️ are you two being serious right now ? If you are going to discuss differences with other chains, be critical of their trade-offs, and put some effort into a good technical question, instead of a generic "opinions on"? Nobody has the time to engage in this stuff. <@!363955106850275331> I looked at cheapETH. There's no optimization there, it's a straight Ethereum clone: The reason that tx are fast there is that it doesn't have the network effects that ETH has; the reason it's cheap is that you can't really trade its token, by design. Think of it as a testnet with a residual value to the token, which makes it more secure than a traditional testnet. It's meant for trying web3 things. I did that too, i was told it was optimized but when i looked at the block explorer i just realized it was cloned ETH with regular gas of 21k per transfer Ultimately, no silver bullet to scaling. Go centralized, or bet on L2 and stay decentralized, as Ethereum is doing. We're soon releasing two bridges in partnership with Polygon Bridge 1 : Decentralized, open, cheap, and almost instant bridge for the transfer of funds between EVM compatible blockchains Bridge 2 : Decentralized, open, cheap bridge for inter blockchain communication of smart contracts We plans to use the second Bridge to fully link L2 solutions and independent blockchains such as BSC and ETH to create a huge interlinked network of blockcahins we hope this would help solve many of the issues currently faced Very cool. Definitely also check https://ethresear.ch/t/cross-rollup-dex-with-smart-contracts-only-on-the-destination-side/8778 Anything that makes L2<->L2 interactions easy(ier) without needing to do L2->L1->L2 is a great help What we're developing is much more efficient than this proposal, this proposal is mostly centralized, slow, and little expensive <@!219015859182632960> if i may have your opinion on something Every link between two blockchains using our bridge can handle 42 nodes who stake the most FT (the token of the bridge) So 21 nodes writing on every blockchain We made it limited to reduce transaction fees and made it 21 to maintain security, do you think security can be maintained with a lower number of nodes ? I am not qualified to have an opinion on that
